newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds slipped on Thursday as a lack of follow through buying at a government bond auction and mild disappointment that German rates were left unchanged punctured earlier optimism sparked by weak German data.

A larger than expected rise in German unemployment fueled a wave of buying of cash bonds by primary dealers, hoping the figures would boost rate cut expectations, but when the futures market stalled they cut their positions, traders said.
"The SVTs (primary dealers) took a beating," a trader at a U.S. house in Paris said. "People went long before the auction, some saw the (bond future) at 129.90, which didn't happen."
"Then they cut their positions," he said.
The head of a French futures brokerage said, "We had good cash buying from primary dealers this morning. After the auction they felt the market was weak and they started to lighten" their positions.
"People don't want to be too long at the moment so we had some profit taking," he said.

Analysts said although the French market remained relatively well supported by domestic investors, who were still buying bonds at the lows for the day, a decline in the U.S. bond market was setting the overall tone.
Joanne Perez, stratgist at Merrill Lynch, said, "The market got quite excited after the German (unemployment) figures and went long before the auction but there was no follow through."
The Treasury said it sold 17.35 of OATs on Thursday with most demand coming for the variable rate TEC 10 OAT. However the overall bid to cover ratio of 2.6 was lower than at recent auctions.

Perez said traders were wary about remaining long at the highs with U.S. jobs figures on Friday which were unlikely to be that helpful. "Independently we're pretty well supported with domestics buying on dips, but you've got the U.S. trend."
A head futures trader at a French bank said he thought the French market "had purged itself" and should rebound unless there's bad U.S. news.

PIBOR contracts lost their early gains after both the Bundesbank and the Bank of France left interest rates unchanged. The March contract climbed as high as 96.65, within a whisker of the contract high at 96.66, but fell back to settle unchanged at 96.60.
The two-year spread widened slightly to 10 basis points from nine yesterday and as low as six earlier in the week.
The key U.S. non-farm payroll release for November, due at 1330 GMT on Friday, was expected to show a 179,000 rise in the number of new jobs created.
Continued weakness in the U.S. bond market ahead of the jobs report dragged the French bond future lower in the GLOBEX session though it bounced off support at 128.80 to trade at 128.94 at 1620 GMT.
Nevertheless, it was a more optimistic day in the options market with more than 12,000 January calls trading at a strike price of 131. The contract expires on December 26.
